Jesus Our Role Model (Part 3)
Existing in the form of God, he emptied himself,
taking the form of a servant. (Philippians 2:6–7)
• Greet the congregation; explain that this lesson in the “Jesus Our Role Model” series is about laying down the right to glory.
• Read the key passage, Philippians 2:5–8, in full; stress “but emptied himself.”
• State the theme: the world’s glory is found up high; Jesus’ glory is found down low.
What is printed on your business card?
At a Roman triumph, a man whispered
in the general’s ear: remember you are only a man.
In that same era, another King rode in on a donkey,
laying down the right to glory.
• Open with the question “one line on a business card”; invite everyone to ask which identity they value most.
• The Roman triumph: Tertullian’s Apology records a man behind the general reminding him, “Remember that you are only a man.”
• Contrast Jesus riding into Jerusalem on a donkey and wearing a crown of thorns.
• Draw out the theme: serving is not lifting ourselves up but laying ourselves down.
Key Passage and Background
Philippians 2:5–8
Written by Paul in prison in Rome, c. AD 60
Philippi: a Roman colony that prized status
The city that loved face receives a letter that cared nothing for it
• Author: Paul, during his imprisonment in Rome (c. AD 60–62); internal evidence: “the whole palace guard” (Philippians 1:13) and “those who are of Caesar’s household” (Philippians 4:22).
• Philippi: a Roman colony where Octavian settled retired soldiers after the great battle of 42 BC; residents prided themselves on Roman citizenship (Acts 16:21).
• The first century was an honour-and-shame culture: a slave had the least honour, the cross was the greatest shame.
• Philippians 2:6–11 is called the “Christ Hymn”; just before it, Philippians 2:3–4 says “doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit.”
Point One: An Office Is Not a Title
An office is a function, not a rank
For the perfecting of the saints, to the work of serving,
to the building up of the body of Christ. (Ephesians 4:11–12)
Exalt the title, and you lose reverence for the office
• Read Ephesians 4:11–12; point out that the purpose of offices is to perfect the saints and build up the body of Christ.
• An office is a function, not a rank; a verb, not a noun.
• Ask: can an office sin? The office cannot; it is people who sin.
• When people exalt titles, the world stops respecting the church and God’s calling.
Emptied Himself: Not Losing, but Laying Down a Right
He did not empty himself of his deity;
he laid down the right to glory
I, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet
(John 13:14) The moon’s light comes from the sun
• Three Greek words: morphē, form (true nature); harpagmos, a thing grasped (clutched and never let go); ekenōsen, emptied himself (poured out).
• Orthodox faith: emptying himself was not subtracting deity but laying down the right to glory.
• Foot washing, John 13:13–15: he did not say “I’m not really the Lord, so I wash feet,” but “I really am the Lord, so I wash feet.”
• The moon’s albedo is about 0.12; it reflects just over a tenth of the sunlight yet lights the night; its greatest danger would be to think the light was its own.
• Optional: Jim Collins, Good to Great — Level 5 leadership: profound humility plus professional will.
Point Two: Five Identities (1)
Brothers and sisters: all of you are brothers (Matthew 23:8)
Redwoods tower over 100 metres, their roots intertwined
Servants: whoever would be great must be your servant
(Matthew 20:26) Life first, then relationships, then ministry
• Background to Matthew 23:6–8: the scribes and Pharisees loved the place of honour, the best seats and being called “Rabbi.”
• California redwoods: the tallest exceed 115 metres, yet roots go only 2–4 metres deep; they stand because their roots intertwine as a forest.
• Baumeister and Leary’s 1995 “need to belong” theory: stable, caring bonds are a basic human psychological need.
• Background to Matthew 20:20–28: the mother of Zebedee’s sons asks for seats; the ten are indignant.
• Greenleaf, “The Servant as Leader” (1970); 321: life first, then relationships, then ministry.
Point Two: Five Identities (2)
Slaves: made free from sin,
having become servants of God. (Romans 6:22)
Bought with a price, we are not our own
The willing servant, ear pierced, stays because of love
• Romans 6:22 has two movements: made free from sin, become servants of God; a person is either a slave of sin or a slave of God.
• 1 Corinthians 6:19–20: bought with a price, you are not your own.
• Exodus 21:5–6: the willing servant’s ear is bored through with an awl — a lifelong mark: I stay because of love.
• Deci and Ryan’s “self-determination theory”: obedience that comes from embracing and internalising a value is the strongest and most lasting motivation.
• 321: selflessness is not having nothing but entering into the fullness of Jesus; Galatians 2:20, “it is no longer I who live.”
Point Two: Five Identities (3)
Prisoners: the prisoner of Christ Jesus (Ephesians 3:1)
Bunyan wrote The Pilgrim’s Progress in prison
Condemned prisoners: made a spectacle (1 Corinthians 4:9)
When Stephen was martyred, the Lord stood up for him
• Ephesians 3:1 and 4:1: Paul does not say “Rome’s prisoner” but “the prisoner of Christ Jesus.”
• Philippians 1:12–13: his bonds advanced the Good News; 2 Timothy 2:9, “God’s word isn’t chained.”
• Bunyan: from 1660, twelve years in Bedford jail; The Pilgrim’s Progress published in 1678.
• Background to 1 Corinthians 4:8–9: the Corinthians thought they already reigned as kings; theatron, a spectacle; epithanatios, sentenced to death.
• Acts 7:55–56: Stephen saw Jesus “standing” at the right hand of God; Colossians 3:1 says seated, here he stands.
Point Three: Lay Down Freedom, Gain Greater Freedom
True freedom is not doing whatever I want,
but letting the Lord do whatever he wants
The jam experiment: four times the choice, a tenth the buyers
Of him and to him are all things. Romans 11:36
• John 8:36, Galatians 5:1, Galatians 5:13, 1 Peter 2:16: freedom and serving are not opposites.
• Iyengar and Lepper’s 2000 jam experiment: with 24 jams about 3 per cent bought; with 6 jams about 30 per cent bought.
• A kite’s string looks like a restriction but is the reason it flies; a snapped string means not freedom but a fall.
• At sea level each square centimetre bears about a kilogram of air pressure; we are not crushed because there is equal pressure within.
• 1 Corinthians 4:7, “What do you have that you didn’t receive?”; Romans 11:36, of him, through him, to him.

Cultivate a servant’s attitude: do all for the Lord

The more we lay down human glory,
the more God receives his glory
